The petitioner is the accused in C.C.No.172 of 2024 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - V, Kozhikode, which arose out of Crime No. 18 of 2024 of Nallalam Police Station,
Kozhikode.

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against him are under Sections 498A and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
The prosecution case is that the petitioner, who married the defacto complainant/2nd respondent on 21.09.2005, has been subjecting the defacto complainant to cruelty, demanding more dowry.
It is also alleged that the petitioner misappropriated about 100 sovereigns of gold ornaments, which belonged to the defacto complainant.
The Sub Inspector of Police, Nallalam Police Station, Kozhikode, has filed Final Report against the petitioner alleging the aforesaid offence.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further stated that all issues with the defacto complainant/second respondent have been amicably settled, 2025:KER:73765        4 pursuant to a mediation conducted at the instance of the Ernakulam Mediation Centre, functioning within the premises of this Court.
For the above reasons, the petitioner seeks to quash the proceedings against him in the aforesaid case.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the second respondent/defacto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. Annexure A3 is the copy of the Memorandum of Agreement signed by the petitioner, the second respondent and two others, in connection with the mediation conducted by the Ernakulam Mediation Centre, as directed by this Court in W.P.(C)No.31417/2024.
As per the aforesaid agreement, all issues between the petitioner and the second respondent, which arose out of their marital discord, have been settled.
The condition No.xix of Annexure A3 deals with the termination of the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.172/2024 2025:KER:73765

sentences.text: It could be seen from the aforesaid condition that the second respondent had agreed for winding up the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner in the said case as part of the terms and conditions of the agreement arrived at in the mediation.

5. The learned counsel for the defacto complainant/second respondent submitted that the termination of the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner is highly necessary to give effect to the mediation agreement signed by the parties concerned.
It is apparent from the facts and circumstances of the case that the issue involved is purely private in nature.

So also, it is highly necessary to terminate the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner to give effect to the terms and conditions of the mediation agreement, and also for ensuring harmonious relationship between the parties.
Therefore, the prayer of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against him, has to be allowed.
6 In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioner/accused in C.C.No.172 of 2024 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - V, Kozhikode, which arose out of Crime No. 18 of 2024 of Nallalam Police Station, Kozhikode, are hereby quashed.
